text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Swedish railroad authorities must increase safety regulations, a report in the wake of a train accident earlier this year says.

- Handelsbanken economist Carl B Hamilton says Prime Minister Goran Persson's plan to cut the working year by 100 hours would cost the country between 60 and 70 billion crowns annually, an analysis shows.
- Dangerous ethylene oxide gas began to escape after train cars went off a railroad track in northern Sweden. The train was on its way to an Akzo Nobel plant in Ornskoldsvik, Sweden.

- Swedish green party member of parliament Ewa Larsson has written another letter to the International Olympics Committee to vent her oppostion about Stockholm's bid for the 2004 summer olympic games.

- Investment company Incentive managing director Mikael Lilius says the group plans to continue investing on the U.S. kidney dialysis care market. The group also has no immediate plans to spin off its wholly owned medical technology unit Gambro which it sees as an impetus for further growth in the industry.
- Not published because of summer industrial holiday.
